name: Omega Church
shortDescription: Northern Ireland-developed church administration software for member records, groups, communication, reports and finance workflows.
suitableContexts: UK and Northern Ireland churches that prefer a locally installed administration system
Church offices needing member, group, reporting and finance tools

pricing.summary: Omega Church publishes one-off, VAT-inclusive prices for Single Site, Multi-Site and Network editions, with an optional annual support-and-updates service. A Lite discount is stated for organisations with up to 250 active records.

tiers.label: Multi-Site
tiers.detail: Install on multiple computers within a church

tiers.label: Network
tiers.detail: Central server and multiple simultaneous users

tiers.label: Lite discount
tiers.detail: Stated for Single and Multi-Site editions with up to 250 active records

pricing.trialDetails: A fully functional 60-day trial is advertised, with no credit card required.

coreFeatures: Data export to Excel, Word or PDF
importExport: Supplier states data can be exported to Excel, Word or PDF
support: One month of support and updates is included
Optional annual support and updates are published
Supplier states its team is in Lurgan, Northern Ireland

uk-purchasing.value: Omega is described by its supplier as designed for UK churches, with support from Lurgan, Northern Ireland.

gbp-pricing.value: Published licence and support prices are in pounds sterling and include VAT where stated.

exports.value: Supplier states records can be exported to Excel, Word or PDF.

technical-administration.value: Network edition requires a church central server; other editions are installed on church computers.

editorial.assessment: Omega Church is structurally different from the cloud-first systems in this directory: its published options are installed Single Site, Multi-Site or Network editions with an optional annual support service. It may appeal where a church wants that locally managed model, but that choice places greater weight on backup, device access, updates, network administration and a clear handover plan.
bestFor: Church offices that prefer a locally installed administration product
Churches needing member records, reporting and basic finance workflows
Teams with a named person able to own device, network and backup decisions
strengths: Published one-off VAT-inclusive licence prices and a 60-day trial
The supplier provides editions for single-machine, multi-machine and network use
The supplier documents operational reporting and export options
limitations: A locally installed product needs explicit responsibility for backups, access, updates and equipment
This research does not establish a current data-processing agreement, accessibility information, imports, migration assistance or integrations
The reported data-export formats should be tested against the church's actual exit and reporting needs
